abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models through forward-only evaluations, but high-dimensional random perturbations can limit optimization efficiency. Sparse perturbations reduce the search dimension, making the selection of informative coordinates critical. We propose Wanda-Importance Sparsity-MeZO (WIS-MeZO), which uses Wanda weight--activation saliency to construct task-conditioned sparse perturbation masks while keeping the pretrained model dense. We analyze support quality through gradient energy capture and relate it to gradient estimation and convergence. Across 16 benchmarks with LLaMA and Qwen models ranging from 3B to 32B parameters, WIS-MeZO achieves higher aggregate scores than MeZO and reaches comparable validation losses in fewer optimization steps. Comparisons with random and magnitude-based sparse perturbations further highlight the importance of informative support selection.
title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization

abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $η>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(η^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.
title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees

abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization estimates descent directions from function values alone, which removes the activation storage required by backpropagation and makes it attractive for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing low-rank ZO methods either parameterize the additive update through Euclidean factors with a non-unique representation, or restrict each finite-difference direction to be low-rank. In this work, we propose to constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen, so the learned update remains rank-constrained throughout fine-tuning. On this geometry, we build a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator that projects a random matrix onto the tangent space, normalizes it to correct the scale mismatch induced by projection, and further propose Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) and its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S. We show that the ambient finite difference matches its retracted counterpart, the normalized estimator recovers the Riemannian gradient in expectation, and ZO-RGD converges under trajectory-regularity conditions. Experiments on LLM fine-tuning tasks show that the proposed algorithms are competitive with strong forward-only baselines across model families and tasks, with gains in several settings.
title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning

abstract: ABSTRACT Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) dominate visual computing, but their electronic implementations face fundamental bottlenecks in speed and energy efficiency. Although photonic alternatives offer a promising route, all‐optical image recognition using CNNs remains challenging in experiments due to the difficulty of implementing effective weak‐light nonlinearities. Here, we demonstrate a streamlined all‐optical CNN architecture with only physically guided, fixed convolutional and trainable fully‐connected layers (FCLs), which circumvents explicit, energy‐intensive nonlinear layers. Our design leverages a fixed multi‐kernel metasurface operator to perform 24 directional‐differentiation convolutions, thus enhancing feature orthogonality and suppressing crosstalk. This preprocessing enables the system to exploit the weak nonlinearity produced by square‐law detection, thereby achieving high experimental classification accuracy: 86.8% on MNIST and 94.8% on ten‐class gesture recognition. The system exhibits high reconfigurability and robustness. Its all‐optical inference core achieves an equivalent computational throughput of 1.13 × 10 5 TOPS and an energy efficiency of 1.88 × 10 3 TOPS/W—surpassing current CNN implementations. At the system level, it achieves an end‐to‐end throughput of 871 TOPS and an energy efficiency of 4.97 TOPS/W, still exceeding advanced all‐electronic devices and paving the way for ultralow‐latency intelligent hardware.
title: All‐Optical Meta‐Convolutional Neural Networks for Reconfigurable Image Identification

abstract: Optical convolutional neural networks (OCNNs) are susceptible to modulation, alignment, and detection errors, which cause the accuracy of a deployed optical–electronic network to deviate from its numerical model. We propose a learnable bit-plane weighted-fusion (AWF) strategy for low-dimensional offline calibration after camera detection. Each 8-bit input image is decomposed into eight binary planes, convolved separately, and reconstructed using eight learnable normalized weights before electronic activation, pooling, and classification. With 5000 MNIST training images, the optical neural network (ONN) using AWF reaches 92.6% training accuracy, 1.9% points above the traditional binary weighted-fusion (TWF) method. The corresponding experimentally measured test accuracies are 90.30% and 88.69%, respectively. Under 5 dB added noise, AWF-ONN maintains 83.84% accuracy, 5.51% points above TWF, while its loss relative to the no-added-noise condition is 6.46% points compared with 10.36% points for TWF-ONN. A two-layer network retains an experimental advantage of 1.12% points. The results show that a low-dimensional calibration of bit-plane contributions can improve optical inference when labeled data or signal-to-noise ratio is limited.
title: Noise-robust optical convolutional neural networks with adaptive bit-plane weighted fusion
